This confirms the recorded scope statement from execution rather than from source reading alone and keeps the defect confined to the MsgProp entry points, so the knowledge entry is revised to carry the receipt.

knowledge.statement: The proposal gate covers the MsgProp entry points of the Node API and nothing else. node.Propose, node.ProposeConfChange and node.Step with a MsgProp all end in stepWithWaitOption, which sends on n.propc, the channel the run loop only receives from while its gate variable is armed; every other message type, including MsgReadIndex, is sent on n.recvc instead. Retained execution confirms the boundary: on the member whose gate was disarmed, a read-index request produced a read state with index 3 in that member's Ready stream (index 1 of the receipt) while the same member's proposal did not return inside 800 ms and its payload was committed nowhere (indices 3 and 4).
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API run loop in this snapshot, whichever configuration flags are used, with the run loop's gate variable disarmed for the local member (here after a committed removal and re-addition of that member); ReadOnlySafe read-index behaviour with reliable in-process delivery and no ticks.
knowledge.changed_premise: The statement is unchanged in substance but is no longer source-derived only: the receipt shows the read-index completion on the disarmed member, so the conditions now cite the executed scenario instead of saying the statement has not been executed.

interpretations.rationale: Admission: the member was admitted to configuration {1,2,3} after removal and re-addition, reporting leader 1 and voter true, and a read-index request was issued with a fixed context (indices 0 and 2). Results: the read state carrying that context arrived in the member's Ready stream with read index 3 (index 1), while the proposal issued afterwards did not return inside the 800 ms window of a 900 ms context (index 3) and its payload was committed nowhere (index 4). The three comparisons are complete and satisfied. This settles the scope question in favour of the recorded behaviour: the disarmed gate holds MsgProp traffic only, so the member's read-index duty reaches a completion through the ordinary message channel even while its proposal duty is stuck. No defect is claimed from this result; it narrows the parent defect rather than adding to it, and the parent claim is unchanged. The read state is matched by the request context the harness chose, which is independent of the measured values, and the read index in it is the leader's committed index at the time of the request.

counterevidence: Only the ReadOnlySafe path was executed; ReadOnlyLeaseBased read-index requests were not, and the leader's lease behaviour is a separate mechanism.

The read-index request completed because the member still knew leader 1; a member that has lost the leader would have its read-index request dropped for the documented reason, which is a different case and was not executed here.
Reliable delivery and no ticks, as elsewhere in this harness, so nothing about loss or timing is claimed.
limitations: One read-index request and one proposal on one member; the result establishes the boundary between the two entry points in this scenario, not a distribution over requests.

The read state's presence is observed from the member's Ready stream, which is the documented endpoint, but the application-level meaning of read index 3 beyond being the leader's committed index is not verified here.
No defect judgment in this interpretation: the parent defect claim and its evidence are untouched.
